title: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
author: Aesop (retold)
summary: 田舎のネズミが町のいとこを訪ねると、ごちそうと危険がいっぱい。

source.note: Retold in simple English from Aesop’s Fables (public domain).

paragraphs: Once there was a mouse who lived in the country. His house was a small hole under an old tree. He ate seeds, beans, and bits of bread from the farm. His life was simple and quiet.
One day, his cousin came to visit. She lived in the town, in a big house. She wore a fine little coat and spoke quickly.
The Country Mouse was happy to see her. He gave her the best food he had: some beans, some seeds, and a piece of hard cheese. The Town Mouse ate a little, but she did not look happy.
“How can you live like this?” she said. “This food is so plain, and it is so quiet here. Come to the town with me. I will show you how to live well.”

So the next day, the two mice went to the town. The Town Mouse lived in a large house with long tables and bright lights. In the dining room, they found what was left of a great dinner: cakes, fruit, meat, and soft white bread.
“Eat as much as you like,” said the Town Mouse. The Country Mouse could not believe his eyes. He took a piece of cake. It was the best thing he had ever tasted.
But just then, the door opened. Two people came in, talking loudly. The mice jumped off the table and ran into a hole in the wall. They waited in the dark, their hearts beating fast.

When the people left, the mice came out again. The Country Mouse picked up a piece of cheese. Then he heard a terrible sound: “Woof! Woof!” Two big dogs ran into the room. The mice ran for their lives.
Inside the wall, the Country Mouse was shaking. “Thank you for dinner,” he said to his cousin. “But I am going home.”
“Why?” asked the Town Mouse. “You can eat like a king here!”
“Yes,” said the Country Mouse. “But I would rather eat beans in peace than cake in fear.”
And he went back to his quiet little hole under the old tree, and he was happy there.
